summary: A first-person excerpt from a novel in which the narrator's brother has been arrested, and the narrator is committed to getting him freed. Ian gives a talk, speaking in his jeans and tweed jacket, linking a bust at Wilson's house to a vast surveillance-industrial complex. Afterward the narrator returns home, where Monica, who has been on local TV news, tells the narrator that the parents want them to move back home, which the narrator refuses.
one_line: A young narrator, whose brother was arrested, hears Ian link a raid on Wilson's house to mass surveillance, then returns home to a dispute over moving back to their parents.
key_facts: The narrator's brother was arrested, and Wheeze texted the narrator about it.
The narrator was committed to getting the brother freed, which the narrator describes as a personal mission.
Ian spoke at a podium still dressed in his jeans and tweed jacket, with his glasses a little crooked and his hair uncombed.
Ian tied the bust at Wilson's house to a vast surveillance-industrial complex that had flourished for decades.
The narrator says the surveillance was now operating on an almost unimaginably invasive scale.
Most of the audience seemed inclined to help after hearing Ian, except for the law enforcement types in the room.
Sarah was setting up her editing equipment in the hotel suite and demanding Ian's presentation slides.
The narrator left unnoticed with a backpack, hiked home, and reached the apartment before curfew without being stopped by cops.
Monica was grading papers when the narrator arrived home.
Monica had appeared on a local television news story recapping the arrest and the Sunday protest.
The TV story ran a two-second shot of Sunday's protest and about twenty seconds of Monica, and ended with the reporter saying "reporting from South Minneapolis."
Monica said, "I wish I hadn't worn that stupid hat."
Monica said the narrator's parents are worried the narrator will get in trouble like Wilson and want the narrator to move back home.
The narrator responded, "This is my home. You told them no, right?"
